George shoots Loker and takes him to a Quaker community in this novel, while the protagonist refuses to tell Legree where Cassy and Emmeline are towards this novel's end. The title character of this novel saves Eva from drowning, winning the favor of St. Clare. The title character of this novel is whipped by Simon Legree for refusing to whip a fellow slave. Name this anti-slavery novel by Harriet Beecher Stowe.

One work set in this country sees one character relinquish his throne to his son, who eventually has an affair with his own son's wife. Another work from this country centers on 108 bandits who occupy the title location. One novel from this country which produced The Outlaws of the Marsh centers on the retrieval of Buddhist scriptures from India and centers on Sun Wukong ["woo- kong"], who is the Monkey King. Name this Asian country, whose classical novels include Dream of the Red Chamber and Journey to the West, which was written during the Ming dynasty.

This author wrote a work in which Mrs. Erlynne claims the title object is hers while at Lord Darlington's. This author created a character who was abandoned in a purse at a railway station, causing Lady Bracknell to disapprove of his engagement to Gwendolen Fairfax, the cousin of his friend Algernon who courts Cecily Cardew. This author of Lady Windermere's Fan wrote of a character who loves Sibyl Vane and stabs the title object painted by Basil Hallward in The Picture of Dorian Gray. Name this author of The Importance of Being Earnest.

In one work by this author, the title character is helped by Gerasim after falling while hanging drapes. This author of The Death of Ivan Ilyich ["ill-yitch"] wrote one novel in which Konstantin Levin marries Kitty. Other characters in that novel include Count Vronsky, and its title character commits suicide by throwing herself under a train. This author wrote a novel in which Pierre Bezukhov marries Natasha Rostova, during Napoleon's invasion of Russia. Name this author of Anna Karenina and War and Peace.

Montmorency is one of these creatures whose idea of life entails lying in slums and is the subject of the subtitle of the novel Three Men in a Boat. The organs of one of these is replaced with human organs in a novel by Mikhail Bulgakov. One of these creatures dies immediately upon seeing Odysseus return to Ithaca; that animal is named Argos and is known for his faithfulness to his master. Name these animals, exemplified by the faithful pet of Dorothy Gale, the animal Toto from The Wizard of Oz.

This author wrote a poetry collection, the first part of which is titled "Where Love is a Scream of Anguish" and includes the poem "A Zorro Man." One work by this author of "Just Give Me a Cool Drink of Water ‘Fore I Die" takes its name from a poem that proclaims that the central action is "not a carol of joy or glee." This author's autobiography recounts her coming of age experience in Stamps, Arkansas, where Mr. Freeman was murdered after having raped this woman. Name this African American author of I Know Why the Caged Bird Sings.

One story by this author sees the narrator fail to find a suitable gift for the girl he has fallen in love with at a bazaar, while Greta recounts the death of Michael Furey to Gabriel Conroy in another story by this man. This author of "Araby" and "The Dead" also wrote a work set on June 16th which features characters such as Blazes Boylan, who manages Molly's singing career. That work centers on Leopold Bloom and Stephen Dedalus, who was introduced in this author's Portrait of an Artist as a Young Man. Name this Irish author of Dubliners and Ulysses.

In one work, this philosopher wrote about a man who questions the title character, who is on his way to charge his own father with murder. This philosopher wrote about a Pythagorean astronomer in Timaeus. This thinker used the allegory of prisoners watching shadows on the wall of a cave in one work. This man advanced his theory of forms in a work that describes the last teachings of Socrates entitled Phaedo. Name this Greek philosopher who wrote The Republic, the founder of the Academy and teacher of Aristotle.

This author wrote of traveling to an isolated mountain with seven terraces, and in another of his works, this author converses with figures such as St. Peter and St. John. In his most famous work, this poet described meeting the lovers Francesca and Paolo as well as Ulysses, who is being punished for his role in devising the Trojan Horse. In that work, Virgil rescues the narrator from three monsters and guides him through the nine circles of hell. That work is found in a trilogy along with this man's Purgatorio and Paradiso. Name this Italian poet of the Inferno, which is part of The Divine Comedy.

One work by this author sees the protagonist get accused of killing a young boy's cat, and that protagonist is later raped twice by her father. The protagonist of another novel by this author marries Halle, with whom she has her sons Howard and Buglar, and Schoolteacher thwarts Paul D's plans of escaping in that novel. This author created Pecola Breedlove in The Bluest Eye, and wrote about the ex-slave Sethe, who is haunted by the spirit of her daughter who she killed. Name this African American author of Beloved.

In one of this author's books, Elaine Risley and her brother Stephen travelled with their father, who was a field entomologist. This author wrote about a woman who is married to Luke and has an affair with Nick at Serena's prompting. Nick tells that character that the Eyes are part of Mayday, a resistance group opposed to the Republic of Gilead, who are coming to rescue Offred from her work as a reproductive slave for the Commander. Name this Canadian author who wrote Cat's Eye and the dystopian novel The Handmaid's Tale.

One figure in this work chooses to be blindfolded for life upon learning that her husband was blind. A central event in this work occurs when Shakuni wins all of Duryodhana's [Dur-yo-da-na's] possessions in a game of dice. Bhima visits a kingdom of Nagas after being poisoned and nearly drowning in this work. This epic culminates in a battle in which Arjuna receives advice from Krisha during the Bhagavad Gita. Name this Indian epic focusing on the conflict between the Kauravas and Pandavas, a counterpart to the Ramayana.

In this work, Mrs. Goddard receives a goose from another character who lives at Abbey-Mill-Farm with her brother Robert. One character in this work must wait to marry until his aunt, Miss Churchill, has died, and Mr. Elton unexpectedly finds a wife in Bath. The title character of this work is rude to Miss Bates, the aunt of Jane Fairfax, and also unsuccessfully attempts to play matchmaker for Harriet Smith. The title character of this novel eventually realizes she loves Mr. Knightley. Name this novel about a certain Miss Woodhouse by Jane Austen.

One story in this collection tells of a detective attempting to find the murderer of a young woman cut into pieces and thrown in a chest, and the culprit turns out to be his own slave in The Three Apples. In another story, a man becomes rich after a police officer's dream tells the man that he has treasure buried under his fountain. In one story from this collection, a ship crew eats a baby roc, and in another story Cassim is killed by the title group of bandits. Name this collection of stories told by Scheherazade that includes the stories of the voyages of Sinbad as well as Ali Baba and the Forty Thieves.

This author wrote one work whose unnamed narrator has an appreciation only for the "sublime and beautiful," and that work's second part is titled "Apropos of the Wet Snow. Sonya follows her lover to Siberia at the end of one novel by this author of Notes From the Underground. The protagonist of one novel by this author has a dream about seeing a horse unable to pull a carriage get whipped to death, and the pawnbroker Alyona Ivanovna is murdered by Raskolnikov in that novel. Name this Russian author of Crime and Punishment.

One short story by this author centers on a boy who laughs upon seeing blood on soldiers faces but is mute when he sees his own house on fire. This author of Chickamauga described a lawyer as being "One skilled with the circumvention of the law" in The Devil's Dictionary. This author wrote a short story in which Peyton Farquhar finds out that it is possible to sabotage a bridge, and is caught in the act leading to him being hanged, but not before he dreams that he has escaped down the river. Name this author of An Occurrence at Owl Creek Bridge.

This author wrote one poem whose narrator pleads the reader to not ask "What is it?" while in another poem, this man contemplated that the world ends "not with a bang but a whimper." The line "HURRY UP PLEASE IT'S TIME" is repeated multiple times in the section "A Game of Chess" in this authors most famous poem. That poem by this author of "The Hollow Men" and "The Love Song of J. Alfred Prufrock" ends with repeating the word "Shantih," and begins "April is the cruelest month." name this poet of "The Waste Lland."

This work includes an allegory of the mother of all prostitutes in the fourth vision of the judgment on Babylon. The author of this book has a vision of seven lampstands, prompting him to write seven letters. The author of this book sees creatures singing "Holy, holy, holy, is the Lord God Almighty" in his vision of the Throne in Heaven. The fifth vision in this work tells of the bride of the Lamb and the New Jerusalem. This apocalyptic book of the Bible tells of God's eventual triumph over the forces of evil. Name this last book of the Bible.

This author wrote a play in which Halvard Solness promises to build his wife a new house with towers, only to fall to his death from that tower. In this author's most famous play, the protagonist's friend Mrs. Linde rekindles her love with a bank clerk at a costume party. That play by this author of Master Builder sees Krogstad blackmail the protagonist for an illegitimate loan she had taken a few years prior and ends with Nora storming out of her marriage to Torvald Helmer. Name this Norwegian playwright of A Doll's House.

The death of a character of this profession prompts Elesin's ritual suicide which Simon Pilkings attempts to prevent in a play by Wole ["woh-lay"] Soyinka. In one work titled for a character of this profession, Jack Burden quits politics after Adam Stanton murders Willie Stark. In addition to a work titled for "Death" and this character's "Horseman," Shakespeare wrote a work about one of these characters who is betrayed by his daughters Goneril and Regan, and commits suicide after the death of Cordelia. Name this type of character exemplified by Lear.

This author wrote one work in which the narrator is curious about the men and women "attired in the usual costumes" aboard the title boat. One poem by this author talks about a ship that has "weathered every rack" and laments that the title character has "fallen cold and dead." This poet of "Crossing Brooklyn Ferry" wrote one poem in which the narrator announces that he "celebrates" himself. Name this American poet of "Oh Captain! My Captain!" whose poem "Song of Myself" appears in the collection Leaves of Grass.

This character consumes a certain a potion that causes its consumer to seem dead, and two servants of this character's family make a series of puns concerning carrying coal at the beginning of the work this character appears in. This character's nurse relays information between this character and her lover, to whom she is married by Friar Lawrence. Other characters that appear in the same play as this "star crossed lover" include Murcutio, who is killed by Tybalt. Name this Shakespearean character who is in love with Romeo.

In a novel of this title, the narrator Eliezer tells of watching Nazis burn truckloads of babies. In a novel whose title features this word, Nicole asks for a divorce from Dick Diver. In addition to that work whose title refers to a "tender" one of these, Dylan Thomas advised to "rage against the dying of the light" in a poem whose title urges the reader to not go into this time of day. Puck restores the love between Hermia and Lysander in a work whose title features this word. Name this time period during which a midsumer's dream occurs in a Shakespeare play.

This author wrote about the affair between Alcee and Calixta while Babinot is away in "The Storm." This author wrote about Louise Mallard, who dies upon learning that her husband had not, in fact, died in a railroad crash. One work by this author of "The Story of an Hour" ends with the protagonist drowning herself where she first tried to swim. This author created the characters Mademoiselle Reisz and Leonce, who is away in New York for much of a novel that opens at Grand Isle, where Robert Lebrun meets Edna Pontellier. Name this female author of The Awakening.

The mother of the male protagonist of this novel marries him to the widow Heloise Dubuc who dies soon after their marriage. The religious Abbe Bournisien has heated arguments about spirituality with the pharmacist Homais in this novel. Hippolyte develops gangrene in one scene in this work. The central couple of this novel move to Tostes and then to Yonville, where the title figure becomes deeply indebted to Lhereux and has many affairs, before ultimately taking arsenic to kill herself. Name this novel written by Gustave Flaubert, whose title character is a woman named Emma.

One antagonist in this work leaves behind the head of Aeschere after killing him. Unferth argues that the success of this work's title character was due to luck. A villager steals a golden cup from a cave towards the end of this work. The title character beheads the corpse of a figure who had been attacking Herot and decides to help King Hrothgar at its beginning. At the end of this work, Wiglaf helps the protagonist battle a dragon which ultimately kills the hero. Name this epic poem about a hero who killed the monster Grendel.

This author wrote of a love square between Don Carlos, Ruy Gomez, Dona Sol, and the title character in Hernani. In one work by this man, a young boy dies while gathering bullets and the Thenardiers steal from dead soldiers. In another novel, the protagonist marries Pierre Gringoire, despite her love for Phoebus. One of his works focuses on prisoner 24601 who escapes and runs the factory where Fantine works, but is still pursued by inspector Javert. Name this author who created Jean Valjean and Esmerelda in the novels Les Miserables and The Hunchback of Notre Dame.

The protagonist of this work uses up the money he had saved to send his child to the St. Chad's school, and one character claims that John's son Matthew was also involved in a crime which led to the death of a racial activist. The protagonist of this novel meets the girl his son has impregnated towards the end, and it opens with Theophilus Msimangu arriving in the Ndotsheni. Characters in this novel include Arthur Jarvis, who works to educate the people of Ixopo. Name this South African novel focusing on Stephen Kumalo's visit to Johannesburg, a work of Alan Paton.

In one scene from this novel, the protagonists build a snowman that looks so much like Mr. Avery they have to give it hedgeclippers and a hat. In another scene from this novel, the narrator gets mad at her cousin Francis and beats him up, even though Aunt Alexandra made her wear a dress. Calpurnia takes the protagonists to church with her, after which the children learn that Mayella has accused Tom Robinson of rape. Atticus will defend Tom, which causes Bob Ewell to attack this novel's narrator, who is rescued by Boo Radley. Name this novel by Harper Lee, centering on the adventures of Jem and Scout.

This author was inspired by his mistress Jeanne Duval to write many of his works. This author of The Painter of Modern Life called the addressee a "hypocrite" in his poem "To the Reader." This poet wrote that "your kisses could resuscitate the cadaver of" the title creature in "Vampire." He is not Coleridge, but wrote a poem about seamen hunting the title bird in "The Albatross." This poet used a body part to represent fear in the section "Spleen and Ideal." name this French poet who wrote the collection The Flowers of Evil.

In one novel by this author, the People of the Mist assist Alex and his grandmother Kate on their quest for the Yeti in the Amazon. This author of City of the Beasts wrote a novel in which Ferula helps a clairvoyant character search for her mother's head, before that character goes into labor. In that novel by this author, Pedro Tercero escapes to Canada with his lover Blanca, the mother of Alba who is loved by the head of the family, Esteban Trueba, the husband of Clara. Name this Chilean author of The House of the Spirits.

This author wrote a novel in which the title character stows away aboard the Grampus before disguising himself as a ghost to scare away mutineers. In addition to writing The Narrative of Arthur Gordon Pym, this author wrote a story in which a mother and daughter are murdered on the title street by an orangutan. The detective C. Auguste Dupin appears in several works by this man. This author wrote about the murder of an old man whose title organ is stored under the floorboards. Name this author of "The Tell- Tale Heart" and "The Murders in the Rue Morgue."

This author wrote of a title character who is engaged to Haemon, who kills himself after his father decrees that she be entombed alive for burying her brother Polynices. In another work by this playwright, the title character's brother Orestes kills their mother Clytemenestra and her lover Aegisthus. This author of Antigone and Electra wrote a play in which Tiresias tells the title ruler of Thebes that it was he who murdered Laius, his father, and married Jocasta, his mother. Name this Greek playwright of Oedipus the King.

This author wrote one work in which Serenus Zeitblom narrates the story of his childhood friend and composer Adiran Laverkuhn. In another work, this author traced the decline of a wealthy German merchant family from Lubeck headed by Johann. In a third of this man's novels, the protagonist travels to a sanatorium to visit his cousin Joachim Ziemssen, but Behrens persuades Hans Castorp to stay at the title location. Name this German novelist of Buddenbrooks and The Magic Mountain.

This technique is featured in the book You Have Seen Their Faces, which was published by Erskine Caldwell and his wife. One user of this technique was depicted in the Honore Daumier painting Nadar Elevating to Art. Joe Rosenthal used this medium to depict four soldiers on top of a hill. Another artist in this medium produced The Terminal and The Steerage, while another portrayed John Lennon five hours before he was shot. Name this medium employed by Alfred Stieglitz and Annie Liebovitz, which involves using cameras.

This work's title character composes a memorial for her fountain pen and fills a decorated laundry basket with shoes. In one scene, carpenters come to fill fire extinguishers. Mr. Dussel pretends to open a dental practice in this book, jokingly examining another character's cavities. The protagonist's family, including her sister Margot, shares a space with the Van Daans, whose son Peter becomes the protagonist's close friend. All entries are addressed to Kitty in, what chronicle written in a secret annex by a Dutch girl who died in the Holocaust?
The Diary of a Young Girl

In one work by this author, Emily is ashamed of her ward Stephen, who is the illegitimate half-brother of Rickie Eliot. Another of this author's protagonists who quits his job at an insurance company and dies from a falling bookcase is Leonard Bast. This author of The Longest Journey wrote one novel in which George convinces the protagonist to break off her engagement to Cecil, while in another Cyril Fielding defends Dr. Aziz from accusations of rape. Name this author of Howard's End, A Room With a View and A Passage to India.

One character in this work has a vision of Nimrod and the Tower of Babel, and this work's author requests inspiration from Urania. One character in this work lives "where peace and rest can never dwell". After disguising as a cherub to get past Uriel, that character transforms into a cormorant and perches upon the Tree of Life, and he claims it is "better to reign in Hell than serve in Heaven." identify this epic poem in which Satan succeeds in tempting Adam and Eve to sin, a work of John Milton.

Mississippi River, and the slave hunter Loker attempts to capture two escapees from the plantation of Arthur Shelby. One of this novel's main characters is sold to transplanted northerner Simon Legree. Identify this abolitionist novel by Harriet Beecher Stowe.

In one work by this man, he rejects definitions of beauty as that which is appropriate, useful, or gives joy to hearing and sight. Another work by this author of Greater Hippias mentions a Sophist who claims "man is the measure of all things." Besides Protagoras, he transcribed several speeches on love in the Symposium. Justice and the immortality of the soul are the subject of Crito and The Apology, which depict Socrates's trial and execution. Name this philosopher who argues for his abstract forms and introduces his "cave" in The Republic.

This man authorized the construction of the military academy at West Point. One of this man's policies was the subject of a cartoon featuring a turtle named Ograbme biting a man. He removed the "midnight judges" from Federal Courts, and supported the Embargo Act. This president nearly doubled the size of the United States by purchasing the Louisiana Territory from France. Name this third president who designed Monticello and is considered the head author of the Declaration of Independence.

In one of this author's works, a minister gashes his forehead on a beam after buying The Arabian Nights. This author of "The South" dissects sentences like "Upward beyond the onstreaming it mooned" in a story where hronir leak from an idealistic planet, "Tlön, Uqbar, Orbius Tertius". In one of his stories an infinite collection of books is arranged in hexagonal galleries, while in another the German spy Dr. Tsun murders the sinologist Dr. Albert. Name this Argentinian author of "The Library of Babel" and "The Garden of Forking Paths".

The authenticity of this man's teachings is verified by the isnad, or chain of narrators. This man rode a winged horse and then toured both Heaven and Hell in the Isra and Mi'raj, respectively. Some of this man's early followers, called ansar, or supporters, helped him after he completed the Hijra. The hadith are attributed to this man, who fled to Medina after being evicted from Mecca for his radical monotheism. Name this man, the last true prophet and founder of Islam.

This work's protagonist fakes a hand injury to avoid having to forge his name on marriage documents. One character leaves the Friends of the ABC, a secret political society, following a debate over Napoleon's legacy. One couple mistreats their adopted child, the illegitimate daughter of a prostitute named Fantine, while spoiling their biological children, Azelma and Eponine. This work's protagonist offers to buy Cosette from the Thenardiers. Inspector Javert chases the convict Jean Valjean across France in, what Victor Hugo novel?

In one work by this author Charlie Wales attempts to sober up to win back custody of his daughter. In another piece by this writer, the black man Jules Peterson is found dead and Rosemary Hoyt has an affair with Dick Diver. In addition to "Babylon Revisited" and Tender is the Night, he wrote a novel in which the narrator dates professional golfer Jordan Baker and the eyes of T.J. Eckleburg and the green light are prominent symbols. Identify this author who told of a reclusive millionaire's affair with Daisy Buchanan in The Great Gatsby.

This man wrote of an "apple bright" that kills his foe in "A Poison Tree." This author wrote about Myratna's death in "Tiriel," the first of his "prophetic books." This author, who assigned Milton to the "devil's party" in The Marriage of Heaven and Hell, asked "dost thou know who made thee" in one work and "what immortal hand or eye / could frame thy fearful symmetry" in another. Those poems appeared in Songs of Innocence and Experience. Identify this British poet who wrote "The Lamb" and "The Tyger."
